_about: ARMORY (Paolo 11/2, rule 302, ask line 289: 'more clothing, more weapons, the whole thing'). The valley's own weapons and armour, each a Battle Brothers ROLE in a Bohemia skin (scavenged, improvised, pre-collapse). THIS IS THE FILE A MODDER EDITS: one entry a piece. tools/bohemia_armory.py writes every entry into the files the game already reads (weapons.json rows, armor.json body/head rows, armour_names.json, armour_looks.json, ours.json pistol_shot.by_row, slices/rig_melee/rig_melee.json), each written row marked 'armory', so the shop, the fight, the loot, the crew screen and the icons all meet it with no new loader. THE NUMBERS: a piece sits BETWEEN two Battle Brothers rows of its own family ('between': [A, B]): its damage, armour damage, armour ignore, durability, weight and value are the mean of A's and B's (damage and percents to the nearest 5, value to the nearest 10), and it fights with A's own skills, reach and rounds, so every number traces to two wiki pages and the piece is its own tier, never a copy. Easier than Battle Brothers comes from TUNING's sliders over every row, not from these. 'carried_by': the brigand kinds whose wiki gear list holds A; in a fight every second man of that kind who drew A carries this piece instead (same family, same hands), so it drops as loot by tier. The shops sell it by its value like every row (a camp the cheap 40 percent, a town the middle, a fortress the top). 'object' is the drawn icon (slices/bohemia_ui_materials.js) for a weapon; an armour piece is drawn on the man as its 'class' (engine/bohemia_wear.js) and named the house way, a word of its own then the object its weight makes it (rule 202(d)). Words draft:true, eighth-grade.
rule: 302 (Paolo 11/2), 272 (the armour he wears shows), 194 (two hands), 195 (no gun is a club), 185 (guns reach two or more, fire at the man beside him), 170(b) (melee is one tile)
_about_round_2: ARMORY 2 (Paolo 11/2, rule 320, ask lines 316 and 317; records/BOHEMIA_ARMORY_THE_WHIP_AND_THE_POOL_POLE_SPEAR_11_2_26.md). Five more keys a piece may carry: 'starter' (on every camp's smith shelf, the camp's junk, whatever the roll); 'prop' (the family prop it is held as, when A's is wrong for it: a whip is held as the chain, never the cleaver); 'lash' (a whip: its blow is LASH, Battle Brothers' Whip page, and its reach is ours.whip.reach, two tiles; Disarm reaches as far); 'tune' (what moves off the mean of A and B, each with its 'why': 'add' adds, 'set' replaces, 'lash_hit_bonus' is LASH's to-hit); 'whip' (what the fight does on a lash: bleed_stacks, read by the fight off the row; VOTE FIXES 11/2 took out stun_pct, cells_per_lash, cuts_hands, gloves_at_armour and crack_nerve, his 'just animate, fuck these weird debuffs', and made Disarm every whip's luck roll on a landed lash, ours.whip.disarm_pct). Battle Brothers' own two whips (the battle whip, the thorned whip) reach two tiles too: the reach is the family's, not the piece's.
_about_round_3: WEAPONS (Paolo 11/7, rule 424(b), ask line 490: 'we need more one-handed weapons, I feel like there's not enough one-handed weapons'; records/BOHEMIA_WEAPONS_EVERY_WEAPON_SHOWS_11_7_26.md). Six one-handers a man finds in a dead Bohemia, each a Battle Brothers role in its own family, each its own model in the hand (tools/bohemia_weapons_every_weapon_shows_11_7_26.py): the tire iron, the golf club, the Bowie knife, the pipe wrench, the tomahawk and the slot machine handle. tools/bohemia_armory.py now only ADDS on a rerun: what a later lane wrote (a price, an own model, an own look) is kept.

weapons.name: Zip Gun
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' knife: the cheapest thing that kills
weapons.line: A pipe, a spring and a nail. One hand. It fires. Mostly.

weapons.name: Snub Revolver
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' rondel dagger: the sidearm that finds the gap in armour
weapons.line: Five rounds, a short barrel, one hand. Kicks like a mule.

weapons.name: Lever Rifle
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' crossbow: the steady shot across the street
weapons.line: A ranch gun. Both hands. Work the lever between shots.

weapons.name: Scoped Deer Rifle
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' heavy crossbow: the one shot that drops a man in plate
weapons.line: Glass on top, a hunter's gun. Both hands. Slow, far, and it hurts.

weapons.name: Sawed-Off Shotgun
weapons.across: Battle Brothers has one firearm, so B is the rifle family (our crossbow), the other long gun
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' handgonne: the cone up close
weapons.line: Both barrels cut short with a hacksaw. Both hands. A wide blast two houses out.

weapons.name: Pump Shotgun
weapons.across: Battle Brothers has one firearm, so B is the rifle family (our crossbow), the other long gun
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' handgonne, the good one
weapons.line: A police pump gun. Both hands. The loudest thing on the street.

weapons.name: Crowbar
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' mace: dents armour, rings the head
weapons.line: Pries doors and skulls. One hand, the man next to you.

weapons.name: Bike-Lock Chain
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' flail: swings over a shield
weapons.line: A chain with the padlock still on. It comes over a shield.

weapons.name: Box Cutter
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' cleaver: opens a wound that keeps bleeding
weapons.line: A warehouse blade. Small cuts that do not stop bleeding.

weapons.name: Framing Hammer
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' one-hand hammer: breaks armour
weapons.line: A roofer's hammer. One hand. Armour folds under it.

weapons.name: Broom Bayonet
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' spear: holds the line, hits first
weapons.line: A knife taped to a broom. Keeps them off you. Fine with a car door.

weapons.name: Pawn-Shop Katana
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' sword: fast and sure, the riposte
weapons.line: Was behind glass at a pawn shop. Sharp for real. One hand.

weapons.name: Splitting Maul
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' two-hand axe: splits shields, sweeps a row
weapons.line: A log splitter. Both hands, no shield. It goes through doors.

weapons.name: Sign-Post Halberd
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' polearm: the hook that pulls a man out of line
weapons.line: A stop sign ground to an edge on its post. Both hands.

weapons.name: Pool Pole Spear
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' militia spear: the cheapest real reach a man can hold, and the funniest (ARMORY 2, rule 320, Paolo 11/2: 'Pool pole spear: this is so fire and so funny... I want this in the game')
weapons.line: A pool skimmer pole with a kitchen knife taped on the end. One tile. It works.

weapons.name: Extension Cord
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' battle whip at its cheapest: the starter whip, reach two tiles (rule 320)

tune.why: the starter: Battle Brothers' whips plus five at the top (his 'a little more damage... slightly more'), priced and worn like a cord off a garage wall (18 batteries, 30 wear), so the camp's junk carries it

weapons.line: Twenty-five feet of orange cord. The plug on the end stings. Two tiles.

weapons.name: Live Wire
weapons.role: a whip that bites with the valley's money: a cord wired to a battery pack

tune.why: Battle Brothers' whips plus five each end (his 'a little more'); the pack on the belt is the price (62 batteries)

whip.why: VOTE FIXES 11/2 (Paolo in the VOTE tab: 'just animate, fuck these weird debuffs, ammo shit'): no stun, no battery a lash; the live wire is its black wire and its spark on the glass and its numbers (the hardest-hitting low end with the barbed wire, 20-35); its Disarm is every whip's luck roll (ours.whip.disarm_pct)

weapons.line: A cord on a battery pack. It spits sparks when it lands. Two tiles.

weapons.name: Barbed Wire
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' thorned whip (the barbarian's): the whip that bleeds the most

tune.why: Battle Brothers' whips plus five each end (his 'a little more'); wire is softer on armour than leather (20 against the whips' 25 to 30); fence wire is cheap (36 batteries)

whip.why: three stacks of Battle Brothers' bleeding where the whip lays two (the most bleeding of the four: bleeding is a number, his 'Battle Brothers creates a bleeding effect'); VOTE FIXES 11/2 (Paolo: 'Bro just animate... don't do the stat shit'): no cut on his own hands, the barbs are drawn, not charged

weapons.line: Fence wire on a stick. Opens them up. They bleed the longest.

weapons.name: Rodeo Bullwhip
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' named battle whip: the proper one, the most accurate

tune.why: Battle Brothers' whips plus five each end (his 'a little more'); plaited leather from the rodeo grounds, built to last (56 wear) and dear (98 batteries); its LASH +10 to hit, the most accurate whip

whip.why: VOTE FIXES 11/2 (Paolo: 'just animate... don't do the stat shit', on the whips): the crack is drawn and heard, no nerve check; its character is the +10 to hit (tune.lash_hit_bonus) and its 56 wear

weapons.line: Plaited leather off the old rodeo grounds. The surest lash, and the loudest crack.

weapons.name: Tire Iron
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' bludgeon: the plain club that knocks a man out (WEAPONS, rule 424(b))
weapons.line: The L-bar out of a dead car's trunk. One hand. Lug nuts and kneecaps.

weapons.name: Golf Club
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' wooden stick, a step up: long, light, it rings a helmet (WEAPONS, rule 424(b))
weapons.line: A seven iron off a golf course nobody waters. Long, light, and it rings a helmet.

weapons.name: Bowie Knife
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' short sword: quick cuts, and the riposte (WEAPONS, rule 424(b))
weapons.line: Ten inches of clip-point steel off a sporting-goods wall. Fast, and it comes back at them.

weapons.name: Pipe Wrench
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' one-hand hammer: plate folds under it (WEAPONS, rule 424(b))
weapons.line: Eighteen inches of red iron off a plumber's truck. Plate folds under it.

weapons.name: Tomahawk
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' hand axe: chops, and splits a shield (WEAPONS, rule 424(b))
weapons.line: A sporting-goods tomahawk, the price tag still on the haft. It splits a car door.

weapons.name: Slot Machine Handle
weapons.role: Battle Brothers' club: a heavy end on a short arm (WEAPONS, rule 424(b))
weapons.line: The arm off a one-armed bandit, the red ball still on it. Pull it on a man.

body.name: a football-pad padded vest
body.line: High school shoulder pads over a hoodie. Light.

body.name: a duct-taped carpet padded vest
body.line: Motel carpet, folded thick and taped on. Soaks a hit.

body.name: a licence-plate padded vest
body.line: Nevada plates riveted over a denim jacket. Rattles when you walk.

body.name: a riot-gear plate carrier
body.line: Metro riot gear. Shoulder guards, a hard chest. Heavy.

body.name: road-sign full riot armour
body.line: Two freeway signs bolted front and back. Very heavy. Very safe.

body.name: a black-band padded vest
body.line: The old crew's vests. A black band sewn on for each one who is not here.

body.name: a surplus padded vest
body.line: Bought the same day from the same bin. The tags are still on.

body.name: a road-dust padded vest
body.line: Bleached by a hundred miles of the 95. The shield patch on the back says where you came up.

body.name: a hi-vis padded vest
body.line: The water district's rubber vest. Silver bands so a pump crew can see you at night.

body.name: an armband work jacket
body.line: Your own jacket, an orange band on the arm, your house number on the back.

body.name: a tool-belt padded vest
body.line: A hardware store's apron vest, every pocket full, the tool belt still on it.

body.name: a funeral-coat plate carrier
body.line: The black coat you wore at the grave, a plate carrier under it, the white flower still pinned on.

body.name: a torn-patch plate carrier
body.line: The line's own carrier. Clean squares where the patches were torn off.

body.name: a trophy-hung plate carrier
body.line: Keys, tags and other crews' patches hung all over it. Everything on it was somebody's.

body.name: a lab-coat padded vest
body.line: The lab coat you ran out in, padded underneath, gone brown. Your badge still opens nothing.

body.name: an ash-robe work jacket
body.line: A long grey coat rubbed with ash. The circle on the back is the picture the screen showed before it went dark.

body.name: a black-suit padded vest
body.line: The collector wears a suit. The padding is so it stays a suit.

body.name: a numbered work jacket
body.line: Orange, a number on the front and the back. The number is what you owe.

body.name: a hide-patch padded vest
body.line: Patched with the hides of what came out of the lab. The teeth on the cord are theirs too.

body.name: a fight-robe plate carrier
body.line: The satin robe the floor sold tickets for, a carrier sewn in. Gold thread, oxblood, old blood.

body.name: a gilded full riot armour

tune.why: Battle Brothers' own golden named body armour, Golden Scale Armor (bb_all/1337_Named Armors.txt: Medium, durability 264 to 300, weight 28, 8000 crowns): plate's hold at a medium weight, the way a famed piece is

body.line: Riot plate under gold leaf, made for one man. The gold is rubbed off wherever somebody hit it.

head.name: a goalie-mask hard hat
head.line: A hockey mask on a padded cap. You still see everything.

head.name: a football riot helmet
head.line: A cracked school helmet with the face cage on.

head.name: a welding-mask riot helmet
head.line: Steel face, dark glass. Hard to see out of. Hard to get through.

head.name: a gas-visor full riot helm
head.line: A riot helmet with the gas mask built in. The best head you can find.

head.name: a names-taped hard hat
head.line: Black tape round the crown. The names of the dead are written on it in silver pen.

head.name: a sun-wrap rag hood
head.line: A sand-coloured wrap for the miles of road with no shade.

head.name: a hi-vis hard hat
head.line: White, a silver band, the water district's drop on the front.

head.name: an orange-bandana rag hood
head.line: Orange so the block knows you at night. It is the only thing the twelve of you share.

head.name: a headlamp rag hood
head.line: A hood with a headlamp strapped on. The dark aisles are where the good stuff is.

head.name: a black-ribbon riot helmet
head.line: A riot helmet with a black ribbon tied round it. The ribbon is the promise.

head.name: a steel-pot hard hat
head.line: The line's steel pot. The band with the unit's number was cut off.

head.name: a hand-print riot helmet
head.line: A red hand on the side. The valley knows what the hand means.

head.name: a respirator rag hood
head.line: The lab issued them for the pens. Nobody knows what you breathe in a pen.

head.name: a bone-cowl rag hood
head.line: Bone-white, the circle stitched on the brow.

head.name: a fur-ruff hard hat
head.line: A hard leather cap with a ruff of dire wolf fur. The wolf was not happy about it.

head.name: a sparring riot helmet
head.line: Red leather headgear over a riot frame. The crowd liked to see your face.

head.name: a gilded full riot helm

tune.why: Battle Brothers' own golden named helmet, Golden Feathered Helmet (bb_all/1337_Named Armors.txt: Medium, durability 264 to 300, weight 16, 6000 crowns)

head.line: A riot helm gilded to match, a gold crest down the crown. Everybody on the road knows the shape of it.

_about_origins: ORIGINS (rule 427(c), Paolo 11/7 via the coordinator: 'every origin starts like itself and gets personal: its own look, things only it can buy, its own way'). A piece with 'origin' is that origin's own: its crew walks in wearing it (records/target/bb/origins.json door kit), and only that origin's home town sells it (engine/bohemia_origin_ways.js reserved(): no other shelf, no loot, no hire carries it). 'own' is its own model on the body (slices/wear, tools/bohemia_origins_their_own_gear.py, rendered through the master rig). Numbers the armory's way (the mean of 'between'), the Lone Wolf's two Battle Brothers' own golden named pieces ('tune'). A modder adds an origin's piece by adding a row with its 'origin'.
